title: Outlet industrial-remnant settlement
scope: Qualitative existence, siting, capability, cultural composition, and story-start rivalry relationship of the initial region's second settlement, built around a reused imperial industrial village nucleus toward the seaward end of the basin's outlet; names, maps, measurements, works detail, resources detail, population, institutions, shore works, events, and all future-conflict and timeline claims remain open.
approval_evidence: During the 2026-08-17 multiple-choice acceptance session the Author directly specified, rather than selected from displayed options, a second settlement built around an imperial industrial village with running water and metals in the hills, grown on its defensible location, water, and industrial capability, lying on the other side of the basin lake from the ridge-spur settlement near the mouth of the outlet toward the ocean, primarily an imperial-remnant community in contrast to the ridge-spur settlement's blended original-imperial culture, with standing tensions and trade rivalry between the two settlements at story start.
question: What second settlement, if any, should exist in the initial region, and with what bounded qualitative siting, capability, cultural composition, and story-start relationship to the initial ridge-spur settlement?
selection: Promote the Author's direct specification as bounded qualitative claims. A second settlement stands in the initial region, built around a reused imperial industrial village nucleus, an instance of WLD-LOCATION-004's reused imperial works node class. Running water gives the site a qualitative water-supply and water-power advantage, and qualitatively workable metal resources occur in the nearby hills. The settlement has grown on the combined strength of its defensible location, its water, and its industrial capability, where grown means only qualitatively larger or more established than a minor hamlet. It lies on the other side of the basin lake from the initial ridge-spur settlement, toward the seaward end of the outlet, near the outlet's mouth toward the ocean, as a qualitative position rather than a mapped location. It is culturally a primarily imperial-remnant community, in contrast to the ridge-spur settlement's blend of original and imperial cultural strands. Standing tensions and a trade rivalry exist between the two settlements at story start, with the standing pressure governed by WLD-EVENT-001. No future conflict, war, invasion, control assertion, or timeline claim of any kind is selected.
alternatives: No option set was drafted or displayed for this record. Following the WLD-LOCATION-001A direct water-disposition precedent for directly added Author content, the Author's 2026-08-17 direct specification was captured and promoted as bounded qualitative claims; no competing option was presented or rejected.
rationale: The directly specified second settlement gives the initial region a bounded counterpart community with an industrial, imperial-remnant character, a contrasting cultural composition, and a governed story-start rivalry, without selecting names, maps, measurements, works detail, resources detail, population, institutions, shore works, events, or any future conflict.
evidence: Author direct specification on 2026-08-17, captured in the promoted proposal
WLD-LOCATION-004, WLD-HISTORY-001, WLD-CULTURE-001, WLD-CULTURE-002, and WLD-EVENT-001, accepted in the same 2026-08-17 batch
consequences: A second settlement stands in the initial region, built around a reused imperial industrial village nucleus, an instance of WLD-LOCATION-004's reused imperial works node class.
Running water at the site provides a qualitative water-supply and water-power advantage; no watercourse, mechanism, or works detail is selected.
Qualitatively workable metal resources occur in the nearby hills; no ore, quantity, or mining detail is selected.

The settlement has grown on its defensible location, water, and industrial capability; grown means qualitatively larger or more established than a minor hamlet, with actual size, population, government, institutions, and economy open and no comparison with the ridge-spur settlement's accepted population range established.

The settlement lies on the other side of the basin lake from the initial ridge-spur settlement, toward the seaward end of the outlet, near its mouth toward the ocean, as a qualitative position consistent with WLD-GEOGRAPHY-001 and WLD-GEOGRAPHY-002, not a mapped location.

The settlement does not touch the outlet throat or mixed-reach feature sequence or the migrant passage records; no claim about migration, passage, or the mixed reach is made, and WLD-ECOLOGY-006, WLD-ECOLOGY-009, and WLD-ECOLOGY-010 stay untouched.

The settlement is culturally a primarily imperial-remnant community, in contrast to the ridge-spur settlement's blend of original and imperial cultural strands; WLD-HISTORY-001, WLD-CULTURE-001, and WLD-CULTURE-002 remain the authorities for the period and the strands, and primarily does not mean exclusively.
Cultural identity and contrast are human self-description and interpretation, not natural System behaviour; the System assigns no cultural category.
Standing tensions and a trade rivalry exist between the two settlements at story start; WLD-EVENT-001 governs that standing pressure, and no incident, event, escalation, or fighting is selected.
No future conflict, war, invasion, control assertion, or timeline claim of any kind is selected, and no claim that fighting will occur is made; plot intent is staged outside setting canon.
The settlement's name, founding date, precise composition, imperial-era function, current leadership, harbour or shore works, and relations beyond the standing rivalry remain open.
The settlement is author-side setting truth and does not become automatic character knowledge.
Ordinary finite land, water, metal, matter, energy, labour, time, maintenance, and recovery remain causal.

No System settlement designation, safe zone, defensive modifier, production bonus, trade mechanic, faction mechanic, reputation value, spawn, reset, automatic repair, free resource, or guaranteed recovery is created, and no CAL0 rule changes.

Later accepted outlet or passage work makes every coherent placement contradict WLD-GEOGRAPHY-002, WLD-ECOLOGY-006, WLD-ECOLOGY-009, or WLD-ECOLOGY-010.
Later accepted history or culture work cannot support a primarily imperial-remnant community consistent with WLD-HISTORY-001, WLD-CULTURE-001, and WLD-CULTURE-002.
